item.stem: The quiz scores (points) are 62, 67, 68, 73, 73, 79, 79, 82, 85, 87, 92, 95. Which representation correctly displays these quantitative data?
item.title: apstat-u1-5-3a-graphs-105000

mcqChoices.choiceText: Bar chart with one bar for each named category of quiz scores, rather than a numeric axis
Histogram with counts 60-69 points: 3; 70-79 points: 3; 80-89 points: 4; 90-99 points: 2; 100-109 points: 0
Histogram with counts 60-69 points: 3; 70-79 points: 4; 80-89 points: 3; 90-99 points: 2; 100-109 points: 0

diagram.body: Each observation is a dot placed above (or beside) its value on the axis, with nearly identical values stacked.

items.label: Dot
items.meaning: one observation of the quantitative variable

items.label: Stacking
items.meaning: nearly identical values are stacked on top of each other

diagram.title: Dotplot

diagram.body: Ordered bins of the quantitative variable lie along the horizontal axis, and each bar's height is the frequency or relative frequency in that bin.

items.label: Bins (intervals)
items.meaning: ordered intervals of values along the horizontal axis (or vertical axis in a horizontal histogram)

items.label: Bar height
items.meaning: frequency or relative frequency of observations in the bin

items.label: Bin width
items.meaning: changing it can change the histogram's appearance

diagram.title: Histogram

diagram.body: Each value is split into a stem (first digit or digits) and a leaf (usually the single digit after the stem), with both ordered smallest to largest.

items.label: Stem
items.meaning: first digit or digits of the value

items.label: Leaf
items.meaning: usually the single digit after the stem digit(s)

items.label: Ordering
items.meaning: stems and leaves both ordered smallest to largest

diagram.title: Stem-and-leaf plot

vocabulary.body: A variable (also called numerical) whose values are numerical for a measured or counted quantity and generally have units of measure.
vocabulary.title: Quantitative variable
